name: Congenital Prekallikrein Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Laboratory-based diagnostic criteria for congenital prekallikrein deficiency

criteria.description: Markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) not corrected by mixing studies
Severely reduced or absent plasma prekallikrein activity measured by specific coagulation assays
Exclusion of other intrinsic pathway factor deficiencies (e.g., factor XII, factor XI)
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the KLKB1 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of markedly prolonged aPTT with severely reduced prekallikrein activity and exclusion of other intrinsic pathway factor deficiencies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Isolated prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic laboratory finding without clinical bleeding tendency
Patients typically lack bleeding symptoms despite abnormal coagulation tests
searchTerms: abnormal blood clotting test without symptoms

common.symptomName: Mild bleeding tendency during invasive procedures
common.notes: Rarely, mild bleeding may occur during surgery or trauma

searchTerms: slow clot formation in lab tests

common.notes: Helps differentiate from other coagulation disorders

occasional.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding time in some cases
searchTerms: slow blood clotting in some cases
temporary low blood pressure during plasma infusion
low red blood cells due to blood loss

rare.notes: Very rare but reported in isolated cases
Rarely associated due to kallikrein-kinin system involvement

laboratory: Markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)
Severely reduced or absent prekallikrein activity
Normal levels of other intrinsic pathway factors (XII, XI)
other: No clinical bleeding tendency in most patients despite abnormal coagulation tests

distinguishingFeatures: Prolonged aPTT with normal prekallikrein activity
Factor XII activity deficiency confirmed by assay
Prolonged aPTT with reduced factor XI activity
Variable bleeding tendency including mucosal bleeding

redFlags: Unexpected bleeding during surgery despite normal PT
Markedly prolonged aPTT uncorrected by mixing studies
Thrombotic events in a patient with coagulation abnormalities
references: Fletcher Factor Deficiency. Orphanet Report Series. Orphanet; 2021.
Mannucci PM, et al. Prekallikrein deficiency: clinical and laboratory features. Haemophilia. 2015.
